transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Lately I feel drained all the time, like I don’t have the energy to get through my workday or even enjoy fishing on the weekends. It’s just been really tough to find the motivation to do anything.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did it start after a specific stressful event or life change?

These cycles of ups and downs have been going on for about a year, but this current low mood has really hung over me for most of the past 11 months. It seemed to get a lot worse after my IT firm took on several new contracts, which forced me into doing after-hours server migrations and on-call support that totally disrupted my routine.
Have your symptoms been mainly tied to that work stress, and do they improve when the stress eases, or have they stayed present most days even when things are calmer?

The work stress definitely made things worse, but these ups and downs have been happening for about a year now, even during calmer periods. This low mood has been hanging over me for most of the last eleven months, regardless of how busy work is. A close friend from my fishing club actually pointed out that my swings seemed like a lot more than just normal stress.

Have you had any period of at least two weeks during this time when you felt mostly back to your usual self, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day for most of the past 11 months?

No, I haven't had any two-week periods where I felt back to my normal self; this low mood and lack of interest have been there nearly every day for the last 11 months. The only real breaks I've had from the depression are those brief, intense bursts where I feel completely revved up. Other than those short spikes, it's just been a constant heavy cloud.
Did your symptoms begin within a few months after the work changes and seem closely tied to that stress, or did they start independently and keep going even when the stress was not present?

The ups and downs actually started about a year ago, which was well before those work changes over the last several months. While the patterns were already there, the new workload and after-hours stress definitely made everything much worse and really brought it all into focus.
Did your symptoms start within 3 months of the work stress and seem directly caused by it, or were you already feeling depressed before that stress began?

I was already feeling depressed and dealing with these cycles before the work stress started. This low mood has been dragging on for about eleven months, whereas the extra work pressure only began a few months ago. The stress definitely made things worse, but the symptoms were already there beforehand.
Did your mood symptoms begin within 3 months after the work stress started, or were you already having these symptoms before that stress began?

I was definitely having these symptoms before the work stress started. The cycles of feeling revved up and then crashing began about a year ago, whereas the intense work pressure only started over the last several months. The new stress just made a pattern that was already there much harder to manage.
When you feel depressed, do you also have several symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, concentration, guilt, or thoughts of death, and do these episodes last at least two weeks at a time?

Yes, I definitely experience almost all of those, and they've lasted much longer than two weeks—I've been stuck in this current depression for most of the past eleven months. I barely sleep or eat, I'm constantly consumed by guilt and feeling like a failure after my work warning, and on my worst days, I even have scary thoughts about not waking up or driving my car into a wall.
Have you had any actual thoughts of killing yourself, or made any plan or intent to act on those thoughts?

On my worst days, I do catch myself thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up, or even picturing driving my car into a wall. I don't have any plan or intention to actually act on them, though. Those thoughts just pop into my head, and they really scare me afterward.

Did the depression and mood changes begin within 3 months after the work stress started, and do they seem to improve when the stress is reduced? Or were you already feeling depressed before that stress began?

I was definitely feeling depressed before the work stress started, since my symptoms began about a year ago and the new contracts only came in a few months back. Also, they don't really improve when things calm down; these cycles seem to happen on their own schedule regardless of my workload.

Have you ever had periods of at least 4 days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, had racing thoughts, or did impulsive things like spending too much or taking big risks?

Yes, I've had those exact stretches lasting about a week, most recently about a month ago. I only slept three or four hours a night but felt completely wired, staying up late working on home automation projects and getting snappy if anyone tried to slow me down. I also went on an impulsive online shopping spree for networking gear we couldn't really afford, which strained our budget.
During those energized periods, did you ever have symptoms so severe that they caused major problems at work or at home, or did you ever need to be hospitalized or have psychosis?

No, I've never had psychosis or needed to be hospitalized, and those high periods didn't cause major, destructive problems on their own. While I did overspend on credit cards and got a bit snappy with people, the actual major problems—like getting written up at work and pulling away from my family—only happened when I crashed into my low, depressed periods.
During those week-long energized periods, did you ever have to be hospitalized, become unable to function at work or at home, or have symptoms like hallucinations or delusional beliefs?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, and I've never experienced hallucinations or delusional beliefs. During those "up" times, I actually felt like I was functioning on overdrive and being highly productive, though I did make some impulsive choices like overspending on gadgets. The actual breakdown in my ability to function and the trouble at work only happened once I crashed into my low, drained periods.

Have you ever had a period of unusually high energy or irritability that lasted at least 1 week and caused major problems, like needing hospitalization, having hallucinations or delusions, or being unable to function at work or at home?

No, I've never had anything as severe as hallucinations, delusions, or needing to be hospitalized during those high times. They usually lasted about a week, and while I didn't lose my ability to function—in fact, I felt overly productive working late on big projects—I did make some impulsive decisions like overspending on credit cards and getting snappy with others.
During those high-energy periods, did the symptoms last at least 4 full days, and did they feel clearly different from your usual self?

Yes, those high-energy periods definitely lasted at least four days, usually about a week or so. They felt completely different from my normal self—I felt unrealistically good, wired, and like I was running on some extra battery.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed, and separate periods of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep?

Yes, my current depressed period has been dragging on for most of the past eleven months, which is way longer than two weeks. Those separate "up" periods usually last about a week, where I feel highly energized, get irritable if anyone questions me, and only need three or four hours of sleep to feel completely wired.
During those high-energy periods, did you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, had hallucinations or delusions, or were unable to function at work or at home?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, had hallucinations, or lost touch with reality during those high periods. In those times, I actually felt highly active and productive, even though I stayed up too late and made some impulsive purchases. The actual trouble functioning and getting written up at work only happened when I crashed into my low, drained periods.
Have your high-energy periods ever been severe enough to require hospitalization, cause you to lose touch with reality, or make it impossible to function at work or at home?

No, my high-energy periods have never led to hospitalization or losing touch with reality. During those times, I actually felt like I was over-functioning—working late, taking on extra projects, and staying up to rewire things—even though I was snappy and spent too much money. The actual trouble at work, like getting written up, only happened once I crashed into these low, drained periods.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms recurrent distinct elevated/irritable episodes lasting about a week with decreased need for sleep, increased energy/productivity, irritability, and impulsive spending, alternating with a prolonged depressive episode lasting nearly 11 months with anhedonia, low energy, poor sleep/appetite, guilt, and suicidal ideation. There is no history of psychosis or hospitalization, and the elevated episodes meet hypomanic rather than manic severity, supporting bipolar affective disorder. Work stress worsened symptoms but did not fully account for the episodic mood pattern.
